title: Degree growth conjecture for homogeneous Gaussian cycle polynomials
statement:
For the $m$-cycle, let $\Gamma_m$ denote the homogeneous cycle polynomial defining the relevant algebraic boundary component. **Homogeneous cycle-polynomial degree conjecture.**

$$
\deg(\Gamma_m)=m\cdot2^{m-3}.
$$

The formula is predicted from the listed degrees for small $m$; the source explicitly states that an exact formula for the degree of the nonhomogeneous polynomial is unknown, and this homogeneous formula remains unproved.
source_name: Bernd Sturmfels and Caroline Uhler, “Multivariate Gaussians, Semidefinite Matrix Completion, and Convex Algebraic Geometry”, arXiv:0906.3529 (2009).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.3529

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2009).

title: Extremal-value conjecture for irredundant families when n equals 2k minus 1
statement:
Let $M(n,k)$ be the maximum size of an irredundant family of $k$-dimensional subcubes of $Q_n=\{0,1\}^n$. Let $O$ be the centre vertex used in the source, and let $\mathcal F_O$ be the family of all $k$-subcubes through $O$. For $n=2k-1$, **extremal-value conjecture.**

$$
M(2k-1,k)={2k-1 \choose k}.
$$

The conjectured extremal family is $\mathcal F_O$, whose size is the displayed binomial coefficient. This is the boundary case relevant to the Aharoni–Holzman problem, since a projection argument reduces the general conjecture to $n=2k-1$; the source presents the equality as conjectural.
source_name: David Ellis, “Irredundant Families of Subcubes”, arXiv:1003.2960 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.2960

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2010).

title: Erdős–Shelah conjecture for maximum union-free subfamilies
statement:
Let $f(m)$ denote the largest integer such that every family of $m$ sets contains a union-free subfamily of size at least $f(m)$, where a family is **union-free** if it has no three distinct sets $X,Y,Z$ with $X\cup Y=Z$. Erdős and Shelah proved the upper bound $f(m)<2\sqrt{m}+1$ and conjectured that it is asymptotically tight.

**Erdős–Shelah conjecture.**

$$
f(m)=(2-o(1))\sqrt{m}.
$$

The paper states that it verifies this conjecture and later proves the exact formula $f(m)=\lfloor\sqrt{4m+1}\rfloor-1$, so the conjecture is solved.
source_name: Jacob Fox, Choongbum Lee and Benny Sudakov, “Maximum union-free subfamilies”, arXiv:1012.3127 (2011).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.3127

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2010); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Minimum determinant conjecture for bivariate Bézier matrix submatrices
statement:
Let $d$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal I_d$ be the set of weak $3$-compositions of $d$, and let $N_\Gamma$ be the matrix considered in the paper for a nonempty subset $\Gamma\subset\mathcal I_d$. For $\ell\in\mathbb N$, define

$$
n_d:=\begin{cases}\ell^{3\ell},&d=3\ell,\\(\ell+1)^{\ell+1}\ell^{2\ell},&d=3\ell+1,\\(\ell+1)^{2\ell+2}\ell^\ell,&d=3\ell+2.\end{cases}
$$

**Exact minimum conjecture.**

$$
\min_{\substack{\Gamma\subset\mathcal I_d\\Gamma\neq\emptyset}}\det N_\Gamma=n_d.
$$

This gives a proposed closed form for the smallest determinant among the matrices $N_\Gamma$, refining the determinant-minimization problem. The supplied text does not establish its status.
source_name: Gasper Jaklic and Tadej Kanduc, “On positivity of principal minors of bivariate Bezier collocation matrix”, arXiv:1106.0631 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0631

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

title: Conjecture on the exact value of the weighted Hajnal–Szemerédi threshold
statement:
For integers $r\geq 2$ and $t\in(0,1]$, let $\delta(r,t)$ denote the infimum of the minimum weighted-degree density guaranteeing a partition into $r$-cliques of total weight at least $t\binom{r}{2}$. **The authors' conjecture.**

$$
\delta(r,t)=\frac{1}{r}+\left(1-\frac{1}{r}\right)t.
$$

The paper introduces this function and proves matching lower and upper bounds only in special or approximate forms, so the asserted exact formula remains open in the source.
source_name: József Balogh, Graeme Kemkes, Choongbum Lee and Stephen J. Young, “Towards a weighted version of the Hajnal-Szemerédi Theorem”, arXiv:1206.1376 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.1376

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

title: The crossing-number conjecture for the crown graph
statement:
Let $K_{n,n}-nK_2$ be the bipartite graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$ by deleting a perfect matching, and let $cr(G)$ denote the crossing number of a graph $G$.

**Crossing-number conjecture.**

$$
cr(K_{n,n}-nK_2)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture gives an exact formula for the crossing number of the crown graph. The paper establishes matching upper and substantially weaker lower bounds in general, and proves the formula for $n=5$; the general equality remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: Yuansheng Yang, Baigong Zheng, Xiaohui Lin and Xirong Xu, “The crossing numbers of K_n,n-nK_2, K_nP_2, K_nP_3 and K_nC_4”, arXiv:1211.4437 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

title: Sills–Wang characteristic-polynomial conjecture for the Wiener-index matrix
statement:
Let $A_k=(a_{ij})$ be the $k\times k$ matrix with $a_{ij}=\frac{1}{2}|i-j|$, and let $I_k$ be the $k\times k$ identity matrix. Define $C_k(\lambda)=\det(A_k-\lambda I_k)$ to be the characteristic polynomial of $A_k$. **Sills–Wang's characteristic-polynomial conjecture.**

$$
C_k(\lambda)=(-1)^k\lambda^k\left(1-\frac{k}{4}\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\frac{j}{j+1}\binom{k+j}{2j+1}\lambda^{-j-1}\right).
$$

The formula gives an explicit expression for the characteristic polynomial and was proposed to obtain sharper information about the largest eigenvalue of $A_k$. The paper proves this conjecture, so its database status is solved.
source_name: Ya-Lei Jin and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “On the Two Conjectures of the Wiener Index”, arXiv:1304.0873 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.0873

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: The conjecture on the complementary bounding function of the almost identity function
statement:
Let $g$ be the almost identity function

$$
g(x)=\begin{cases}
3 & \text{for } x=2,\\
x & \text{for } x>2.
\end{cases}
$$

For a graph $G$, let $\alpha(G)$ be its independence number and let $\theta(G)$ be its minimum clique-cover number. The complementary bounding function $g^*$ is the optimal function bounding $\theta(G)$ in terms of $\alpha(G)$ for graphs whose chromatic number is bounded by $g(\omega(G))$. **The conjecture on $g^*$.**

$$
g^*(x)=\left\lfloor\frac{8}{5}x\right\rfloor.
$$

The statement is suggested by the preceding upper bound and is presented as a conjectural formula; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it is recorded as open.
source_name: András Gyárfás, Zhentao Li, Raphael Machado, András Sebo, Stéphan Thomassé and Nicolas Trotignon, “Complements of nearly perfect graphs”, arXiv:1304.2862 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.2862

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2013). “This conjecture remains open even for $c=1$.”

title: Characterization of inner products by phase covariance
statement:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be a complex normed space, and let $\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\rangle$ denote the product induced by the norm through the polarization formula. For every phase $e^{{\bf i}\cdot\varphi}$ on the complex unit circle and all $\vec x,\vec y\in X$, consider the covariance identity

$$
\left\langle e^{{\bf i}\cdot\varphi}\cdot\vec x\mid\vec y\right\rangle=e^{{\bf i}\cdot\varphi}\cdot\left\langle\vec x\mid\vec y\right\rangle.
$$

**Phase-covariance characterization.** This identity holds for all $\vec x,\vec y\in X$ if and only if the product $\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\rangle$ is an inner product, so that $(X,\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\rangle)$ is an inner-product space. The claim would characterize inner-product spaces by the expected complex homogeneity of the induced product. The source gives a counterexample showing that the identity can fail in the supremum norm, but does not establish the stated equivalence in general.
source_name: Volker W. Thürey, “The Complex Angle in Normed Spaces”, arXiv:1308.5412 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.5412

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2013).

title: Erd s–Simonovits even-cycle extremal-number conjecture
statement:
Let $\ell\geqslant2$, and write

$$
\operatorname{ex}\bigl(n,\{C_3,C_4,\ldots,C_{2\ell}\}\bigr)
$$

for the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing none of the cycles $C_3,C_4,\ldots,C_{2\ell}$. **Erd	s–Simonovits conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}\bigl(n,\{C_3,C_4,\ldots,C_{2\ell}\}\bigr)=\Theta\bigl(n^{1+1/\ell}\bigr).
$$

The source invokes this conjecture conditionally to show that the bounds of its random Tur	n theorem are essentially best possible.
source_name: Robert Morris and David Saxton, “The number of C_2l-free graphs”, arXiv:1309.2927 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2927

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

title: Anand's conjecture on minimizers of the nonlocal strain-gradient plasticity energy
statement:
Let $\ell$ and $h$ be the material length-scale and specimen height, respectively, and let $\mathcal{T}(f)$ be the energy functional

$$
\mathcal{T}(f):=\frac{S_0}{h}\int_0^h\sqrt{f(y)^2+\ell^2|f_{,y}(y)|^2}\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$

Let the space of admissible functions, the yield strength $\tau$, and Equation~ be as specified in the paper. **Anand's conjecture.** The energy $\mathcal{T}$ has a minimum value over the space of admissible functions. Moreover, this minimum value equals the yield strength $\tau$, and every minimizing function satisfies Equation~. The paper's stated purpose is to disprove this conjecture when $\ell/h>\sqrt{2}-1/2$ by showing that solutions to Equation~ cannot minimize the associated energy.
source_name: Jordan S. Cotler and Felipe Hernandez, “Resolution of a Conjecture in Nonlocal Strain-gradient Plasticity”, arXiv:1310.3426 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.3426

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: The centralizer conjecture for normal pairs of fusion systems
statement:
Let $((S,\mathcal{F}),(T,\mathcal{E}))$ be a normal pair of fusion systems realized by a normal pair $(G,H)$ of finite groups. Write $O_{p'}(H)$ for the largest normal subgroup of $H$ of order prime to $p$, and let $C_S(\mathcal{E})$ and $C_G(H)$ denote the corresponding centralizers. **Centralizer conjecture.** If $O_{p'}(H)=1$, then

$$
C_S(\mathcal{E})=C_G(H)\cap S.
$$

This is proposed as a fusion-system generalization of the $Z^*$-theorem. The source reports that attempts to construct a counterexample had failed, but the parser marks the conjecture as disproved; the nature of that disproof should be checked.
source_name: Jason Semeraro, “Centralizers of Subsystems of Fusion Systems”, arXiv:1402.4981 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4981

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2014). “So far, all attempts to construct a counterexample to this conjecture have failed.”

title: The maximum-point conjecture for maximal intersecting families
statement:
Let $N(k)$ denote the maximum number of points in a maximal intersecting family of $k$-sets. **Maximum-point conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$,

$$
N(k)=2k-2+\frac{1}{2}\binom{2k-2}{k-1}.
$$

Hanson and Toft proved the equality for $2\leq k\leq 4$. Tuza's constructions for $1$-critical uniform families do not disprove the conjecture because those families are not maximal intersecting families; the assertion remains open for general $k$.
source_name: Kaushik Majumder, “On the maximum number of points in a maximal intersecting family of finite sets”, arXiv:1402.7158 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.7158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

title: Loehr–Warrington nonstandard $q$-binomial formula conjecture
statement:
Fix $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\mathrm{R}(a,b)$ be the set of partitions fitting in the $b\times a$ rectangle, let $\mathsf{ml}_{b,a}(\mu)$ be the minimum level on the frontier of $\mu$, and let $h^+_{b,a}(\mu)$ and $h^-_{b,a}(\mu)$ be the corresponding arm–leg statistics. **Nonstandard $q$-binomial formula conjecture.**

$$
\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{a+b}{a,b}_q=\sum_{\mu\in\mathrm{R}(a,b)}q^{|\mu|+\mathsf{ml}_{b,a}(\mu)+h^+_{b,a}(\mu)}=\sum_{\mu\in\mathrm{R}(a,b)}q^{|\mu|+\mathsf{ml}_{b,a}(\mu)+h^-_{b,a}(\mu)}.
$$

This gives a proposed combinatorial interpretation of the $q$-binomial coefficient without a coprimality assumption; the supplied text does not state its resolution.
source_name: Drew Armstrong, Nicholas A. Loehr and Gregory S. Warrington, “Rational parking functions and Catalan numbers”, arXiv:1403.1845 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1845

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2014). “The Shuffle Conjecture (which is still open) gives such a precise description.”

title: Maximality conjecture for a family of $p^k$-central spaces
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $d=p^k$, and let $A=F[x,y]$ be a cyclic algebra of degree $d$. For some $0\leq e\leq k-1$, set

$$
V=F[x^{p^e}]y+F[y^{p^{k-e}}]x.
$$

This space is $p^k$-central: every element has its $p^k$th power in $F$.

**Maximality conjecture.** The $p^k$-central space $V$ is maximal with respect to inclusion.

The preceding proposition establishes that $V$ is $p^k$-central, while the supplied text does not prove its maximality or provide a counterexample. Thus the conjectural part concerns maximality among $p^k$-central subspaces.
source_name: Adam Chapman, “p-Central Subspaces of Central Simple Algebras”, arXiv:1406.0069 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.0069

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2014).

title: White's sharp Hausdorff-dimension conjecture for cone stratifications
statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a compact family of closed cones. Suppose that at each point of a set $S$, each blow-up of $S$ is contained in some element of $\mathcal{C}$. Let $d$ be the largest possible Hausdorff dimension of $S$. **White's sharp stratification conjecture.** The number $d$ equals the largest dimension of a linear subspace that is a subset of one of the cones in $\mathcal{C}$. The conjecture would sharpen White's stratification theorem, which gives only that $d$ is at most the largest building dimension of the cones in $\mathcal{C}$. The source explicitly states that a counterexample, together with the stratification theorem, gives an indirect proof that this conjecture is not valid.
source_name: Andrea Marchese, “On the building dimension of closed cones and Almgren's stratification principle”, arXiv:1408.2398 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.2398

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2014).

title: Lower bound for the dimension function of intersected factor posets
statement:
Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be factor posets, and let $calD(P)$ denote the smallest dimension in which a frame with factor poset $P$ has an inverse. **Lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{D}(P_1\cap P_2)\geq \min\{\mathcal{D}(P_1),\mathcal{D}(P_2)\}.
$$

The preceding examples show that the dimension of an intersection cannot be bounded above easily; this conjecture proposes a general lower bound. No proof or resolution is given in the source.
source_name: Alice Z. -Y. Chan, Martin S. Copenhaver, Sivaram K. Narayan, Logan Stokols and Allison Theobold, “On Structural Decompositions of Finite Frames”, arXiv:1411.6138 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6138

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

title: The exact formula conjecture for the topological Tverberg threshold
statement:
Let $N_r(d)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every continuous map from the $N$-simplex to $\mathbb{R}^d$ identifies points from $r$ pairwise disjoint faces. The parameters satisfy $r\ge 2$ and $d\ge 1$.

**Exact formula conjecture.**

$$
N_r(d)=\begin{cases}(r-1)(d+1)&\text{if }r\text{ is a power of a prime or }d\le r,\\r(d+1)-1&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
$$

This predicts the precise threshold governing the failure of the topological Tverberg phenomenon. The supplied text does not provide evidence resolving the conjecture.
source_name: Pavle V. M. Blagojević, Florian Frick and Günter M. Ziegler, “Barycenters of Polytope Skeleta and Counterexamples to the Topological Tverberg Conjecture, via Constraints”, arXiv:1510.07984 (2019).

title: The FJRW effective-algorithm conjecture for quintic singularities
statement:
Let $\Theta_{g,k}$ denote the genus $g$ FJRW invariant of the Fermat quintic with $k$ many $\frac{2}{5}$-insertions. Let $\gamma$ be a tuple of markings from the narrow sectors, and consider the localization relations with $d_0=0$.

**FJRW effective-algorithm conjecture.** The polynomial relations among the FJRW invariants $\Theta_{g,k}$ obtained from these localization relations, with

$$
\gamma\in(\boldsymbol{\mu}_5^{\mathrm{nar}})^{\times\ell},
$$

can effectively evaluate all $\Theta_{g,k}$.

This proposes using nontrivial marking data to determine the complete collection of FJRW invariants, beyond the ranges already covered by the stated theorems.
source_name: Huai-Liang Chang, Jun Li, Wei-Ping Li and Chiu-Chu Melissa Liu, “An effective theory of GW and FJRW invariants of quintics Calabi-Yau manifolds”, arXiv:1603.06184 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06184

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

title: Krattenthaler–Müller's two-row formula conjecture for NPS average complexity
statement:
Let $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ be a partition with two parts, and let $C(\lambda)$ denote the average number of exchanges performed by the Novelli–Pak–Stoyanovskii algorithm on a filling of shape $\lambda$. For $k\geq 0$, define the Pochhammer symbol by $(x)_0=1$ and $(x)_k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$ for positive integers $k$.

**Krattenthaler–Müller's two-row formula conjecture.** The average case complexity is

$$
C(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda_1(\lambda_1-1)}{4}+\frac{\lambda_2(\lambda_2-3)}{4}-2\sum_{k=1}^{\lambda_2}\binom{\lambda_2}{k}\frac{(-1)^k(2k-2)!}{(\lambda_1-\lambda_2+2)_{2k-1}}.
$$

This is an exact formula for the average complexity when the partition has two parts. The source presents it as the third conjecture from private communication; no resolution is supplied here.
source_name: Carsten Schneider and Robin Sulzgruber, “Asymptotic and exact results on the complexity of the Novelli-Pak-Stoyanovskii algorithm”, arXiv:1606.07597 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07597

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

title: Width-minimizing positions that fail to minimize trunk or bridge number
statement: Let $K$ and $K'$ be knots, with embeddings $k$ and $k'$, respectively. An embedding is width-minimizing when it realizes the knot's minimum width; similarly, trunk-minimizing and bridge-minimizing embeddings realize the minimum trunk and bridge number. **Proposed counterexample conjecture.** There exists a knot $K$ with an embedding $k$ that minimizes width but minimizes neither trunk nor bridge number, and there exists a knot $K'$ with an embedding $k'$ that minimizes both width and bridge number but does not minimize trunk. The paper gives concrete examples likely to satisfy this claim, but explicitly stops short of proving that the relevant embeddings minimize width.
source_name: Derek Davies and Alexander Zupan, “Natural properties of the trunk of a knot”, arXiv:1608.00019 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.00019

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2016).

title: General maximum-root bound for the mixed characteristic polynomial
statement:
Let $M_n(\mathbb{C})^{+}$ denote the positive semidefinite $n\times n$ complex matrices, and let a **positive contraction** be a positive semidefinite matrix bounded above by the identity. For $r\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$, let $\chi_r[A]$ denote the $r$-characteristic polynomial of $A$, and let $\operatorname{max root}\chi_r[A]$ be its largest root. If $A\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^{+}$ is a positive contraction whose diagonal entries are all at most $\delta$, then **the mixed-determinant root bound conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{max root}\chi_r[A]\leq \frac{1}{r}\left(\sqrt{1-\delta}+\sqrt{(r-1)\delta}\right)^2.
$$

The text presents this as a plausible estimate for general $r$, following proved estimates for $r=2,3,4$; its resolution is not supplied here.
source_name: Jonathan Leake and Mohan Ravichandran, “Mixed Determinants and the Kadison-Singer problem”, arXiv:1609.04195 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

title: The outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture
statement:
A $2$-coloring assigns each vertex a red usage in $[0,1]$, with blue usage $1-r(v)$; the defect of a vertex is the sum, over its neighbors, of the overlap in their color usages, and $D(G,2)$ is the minimum possible maximum defect over all such colorings of $G$. **Outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture.** For any outerplanar graph $G$,

$$
D(G,2)<2.
$$

Ordinary $2$-colorings of outerplanar graphs have defect at most $2$, and the fan examples show that the minimum defect can approach $2$ from below. The conjecture asks whether the bound is always strictly improvable.
source_name: Wayne Goddard and Honghai Xu, “Colorings with Fractional Defect”, arXiv:1702.01442 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01442

title: Piśniak's distinguishing-index conjecture for 2-connected graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph. Its **distinguishing index** $D'(G)$ is the least number of labels in an edge labeling preserved only by the identity automorphism. Write $\Delta(G)$ for its maximum degree.

**Piśniak's conjecture.** If $G$ is a $2$-connected graph, then

$$
D'(G)\leq 1+\lceil \sqrt{\Delta(G)}\rceil.
$$

This conjecture gives a substantially sharper upper bound for the distinguishing index of 2-connected graphs than the general maximum-degree bounds discussed in the paper. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
source_name: Saeid Alikhani and Samaneh Soltani, “An upper bound on the distinguishing index of graphs with minimum degree at least two”, arXiv:1702.03524 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03524

title: Kawasaki's capacity equality conjecture for stably non-displaceable subsets
statement:
Let $X$ be a stably non-displaceable compact subset of a closed symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$. **Kawasaki's conjecture.** For any $R>0$ and $\ell\in\mathbb{Z}$, one has

$$
C(M,X;R,0,\ell,-\infty)=R\lvert\ell\rvert.
$$

This conjecture proposes an exact formula for the relative symplectic capacity associated with stably non-displaceable subsets; it generalizes the capacity equality established in the torus case, while its validity in the stated generality remains open.
source_name: Morimichi Kawasaki and Ryuma Orita, “Computation of annular capacity by Hamiltonian Floer theory of non-contractible periodic trajectories”, arXiv:1703.01730 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.01730

title: The minimum codegree conjecture for perfect matchings in $K_4^3$-free 3-graphs
statement:
Let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph, where $n$ is sufficiently large and divisible by $3$. Write $\delta_2(H)$ for its minimum codegree, and let $K_4^3$ denote the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on four vertices. A perfect matching is a collection of vertex-disjoint edges covering all vertices of $H$.

**$K_4^3$-free matching conjecture.** For any $\gamma>0$, for sufficiently large $n\in 3\mathbb{N}$, if $H$ contains no copy of $K_4^3$ and

$$
\delta_2(H)\geq \left(\frac{1}{3}+\gamma\right)n,
$$

then $H$ contains a perfect matching.

The examples preceding the conjecture show that the constant $1/3$ is a natural lower-bound barrier for the minimum codegree. The supplied source gives no information about whether the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Jie Han, “On Perfect Matchings and tilings in uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1705.00990 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.00990

title: Butterfly trace conjecture
statement:
Let $B$ be the butterfly poset on four elements $a,b,c,d$, with $a,b<_B c,d$. For a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$, let $Tr_{n-1}(n,B)$ denote the maximum size of a family whose traces on all $(n-1)$-subsets contain no copy of $B$. **Butterfly trace conjecture.** If $n\geq 5$, then

$$
Tr_{n-1}(n,B)=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper proves the related exact formula $Tr(n,B)=\lfloor 3n/2\rfloor+1$, but the asserted value for traces on $(n-1)$-subsets is posed as an open problem.
source_name: Dániel Gerbner, Balázs Patkós and Máté Vizer, “Forbidden subposet problems for traces of set families”, arXiv:1706.01212 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01212

title: Dvořák–Mohar–Šámal's six-color conjecture for subcubic graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a **subcubic graph**, meaning a graph of maximum degree at most $3$, and let $\chi_{\mathrm{st}}'(G)$ denote its star chromatic index.

**Dvořák–Mohar–Šámal's conjecture.** Every subcubic graph satisfies

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{st}}'(G)\le 6.
$$

The preceding results establish the upper bound $7$, while examples with star chromatic index $6$ show that a bound of $6$ would be best possible. No subcubic graph requiring $7$ colors is known, so the conjecture remains open.
source_name: Borut Lužar, Martina Mockovčiaková and Roman Soták, “Note on list star edge-coloring of subcubic graphs”, arXiv:1709.03293 (2017).
references:

title: Bergeron's positivity and unimodality conjecture for q-binomial differences
statement:
Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive integers such that $a$ is the smallest and $ad=bc$. The $q$-binomial coefficient is

$$
\binom{m+n}{m}_q=\frac{(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^{m+n})}{(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^m)\cdot(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^n)}.
$$

Thus $\binom{m+n}{m}_q$ is a symmetric polynomial in $q$. **Bergeron's positivity and unimodality conjecture.** The coefficients of the symmetric polynomial

$$
\binom{b+c}{b}_q-\binom{a+d}{d}_q
$$

are nonnegative and unimodal. This extends Bergeron's positivity problem, which asks whether these coefficients are always nonnegative. The conjecture is proved combinatorially in the cases $a\leq 3$ and $b,c\geq 4$; the general assertion remains open.
source_name: Fabrizio Zanello, “On Bergeron's positivity problem for q-binomial coefficients”, arXiv:1709.06187 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

title: General bipartite graph conjecture for Gallai-Ramsey numbers
statement:
Let $H$ be a connected bipartite graph, let $R(H,H)=R$ be its two-color Ramsey number, and let $s(H)$ denote the parameter used in the source. **The general bipartite Gallai-Ramsey conjecture.**

$$
gr_k(K_3:H)=R+(s(H)-1)(k-2).
$$

This proposes a broad exact formula for Gallai-Ramsey numbers of connected bipartite graphs, extending the paper's bounds and examples. The source does not specify the definition of $s(H)$ or report a resolution.
source_name: Haibo Wu, Colton Magnant, Pouria Salehi Nowbandegani and Suman Xia, “All partitions have small parts - Gallai-Ramsey numbers of bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1710.10455 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10455

title: The conjecture that the minimum is attained at two copies of 2
statement:
For a fixed integer $p\geq4$, let $F_v(a_1,\ldots,a_s;q)$ denote the vertex Folkman number, and let $2_r$ denote $r$ occurrences of $2$. **The minimum-attainment conjecture.**

$$
\min_{r\geq2}\left\{F_v(2_r,p;r+p-1)-r\right\}=F_v(2,2,p;p+1)-2,
$$

that is, $r'_0(p)=2$, and

$$
F_v(2_r,p;r+p-1)=F_v(2,2,p;p+1)+r-2,\qquad r\geq2.
$$

The claim proposes an exact formula for this family of vertex Folkman numbers; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
source_name: Aleksandar Bikov, “Computation and Bounding of Folkman Numbers”, arXiv:1806.09601 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.09601

title: The modular Erdős–Burgess constant conjecture
statement:
Let $n>1$ be an integer, and let $R=\mathbb{Z}_n$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. The **modular Erdős–Burgess constant conjecture.**

$$
{\rm I}(\mathcal{S}_R)={\rm D}(R^{\times})+\Omega(n)-\omega(n).
$$

This conjecture gives an exact formula for the Erdős–Burgess constant of the multiplicative semigroup of $R$. The formula is proved in the paper when $n$ is a prime power or a product of distinct primes, but remains open for general $n$.
source_name: Jun Hao, Haoli Wang and Lizhen Zhang, “On the modular Erdős-Burgess constant”, arXiv:1807.07266 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.07266

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

title: Hamidoune's atom cardinality conjecture for torsion-free groups
statement: Let $G$ be a torsion-free group, let $C$ be a finite subset of $G$ containing the identity element, and let $n$ be a positive integer. For a finite subset $X\subseteq G$, write $\partial_C(X)=XC\setminus X$, let $\kappa_n(C)$ be the minimum of $|\partial_C(X)|$ over finite $X\subseteq G$ with $|X|\geq n$, and let an $n$-atom of $C$ be an $n$-critical set of minimal cardinality; denote its cardinality by $\alpha_n(C)$. **Hamidoune's conjecture.** Every $n$-atom of $C$ has cardinality $n$, that is, $|\alpha_n(C)|=n$. The conjecture is known for unique product groups and for $n=1$, but remains open in general; attempts to prove it even for $n=2$ have been unsuccessful.
source_name: Alireza Abdollahi and Fatemeh Jafari, “Cardinality of product sets in torsion-free groups and applications in group algebras”, arXiv:1808.08708 (2019).
references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2018). “Conjecture is still open and attempts to confirm it even for $ n=2 $ were unsuccessful see e.g.”

title: Wang–Hou's conjecture on sums of signed-graph Laplacian eigenvalues
statement:
Let $G_\sigma$ be a signed graph obtained from a simple graph $G$, and let $L_{G_\sigma}=D(G)-A(G_\sigma)$ be its signed-graph Laplacian matrix. For $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\in[n]$, let $\mu_1(L_{G_\sigma})\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n(L_{G_\sigma})$ be the Laplacian eigenvalues of $G_\sigma$. **Wang–Hou's conjecture.** one has

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mu_i(L_{G_\sigma})\leq e(G)+\binom{k+1}{2}+1.
$$

The conjecture concerns an upper bound for the sum of the $k$ largest Laplacian eigenvalues of a signed graph. The paper's abstract states that it gives a counterexample to this conjecture, so the database status is refuted.
source_name: Asghar Bahmani, “A counterexample to a conjecture of Wang and Hou on signed graphs”, arXiv:1809.08594 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08594

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Jones's conjecture on level-$(p,q)$ Furuta–Mahowald classes
statement:
Let a **level-$(p,q)$ Furuta--Mahowald class** mean the class considered in the paper, with $p$ and $q$ its level parameters. **Jones's conjecture.** For $p\geq 2$, a level-$(p,q)$ Furuta--Mahowald class exists if and only if

$$
q \geq \begin{cases} 2p+2 & p\equiv 1 \pmod 4,\\ 2p+2 & p\equiv 2 \pmod 4,\\ 2p+3 & p\equiv 3 \pmod 4,\\ 2p+4 & p\equiv 4 \pmod 4. \end{cases}
$$

The conjecture proposes the precise existence threshold after the bound $q\geq 3p$ was disproved by a counterexample at $p=5$; its resolution would determine the answer to the existence question for these equivariant stable homotopy classes.
source_name: Michael J. Hopkins, Jianfeng Lin, XiaoLin Danny Shi and Zhouli Xu, “Intersection Forms of Spin 4-Manifolds and the Pin(2)-Equivariant Mahowald Invariant”, arXiv:1812.04052 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04052

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

title: Subcubic red-blue decomposition conjecture
statement: Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning that its maximum degree is at most $3$, and suppose that $G$ has at least $7$ vertices. In a red-blue vertex coloring, the induced blue components and induced red components are the connected components of the corresponding color-induced subgraphs. **Subcubic decomposition conjecture.** Every such graph has a red-blue vertex coloring in which every blue component is a vertex or an edge, while every red component has minimum degree at least $1$ and contains no path with $3$ edges. The authors present this as a slight strengthening of Thomassen's conjecture and state that they have found no counterexample among subcubic graphs; its general validity remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: János Barát, “Decomposition of cubic graphs related to Wegner's conjecture”, arXiv:1901.11339 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.11339

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2019). “Therefore, it remains open whether the conjectured phenomenon in Conjecture generalizes to higher degrees.”

title: Nikiforov's conjecture on the Lagrangian of colex hypergraphs
statement:
Let $r$-graphs be finite uniform hypergraphs, let $\lambda(m,r)$ denote the maximum Lagrangian of an $r$-graph with $m$ edges, and let $\binom{x}{r}$ be the generalized binomial coefficient for real $x$. **Nikiforov's conjecture.** Let $r \ge 3$. If $m = \binom{x}{r}$ for some real $x$ satisfying $x \ge r-1$, then

$$
\lambda(m,r) \le m x^{-r},
$$

with equality if and only if $x \in \mathbb{N}$. Nikiforov proved this for $3 \le r \le 5$ and sufficiently large $m$, while the general case is not resolved.
source_name: Vytautas Gruslys, Shoham Letzter and Natasha Morrison, “Lagrangians of Hypergraphs II: When colex is best”, arXiv:1907.09797 (2020).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1803.08653](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08653).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09797
